ratings_why.fun: Ordering puzzles (who Vane points at, the slot by The Helm, when High Pressure dies) give every turn a decision, though fights will take effort to follow.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because Late makes the hand a second board that lands mid-fight, which no current tribe or typical auto-battler does, and Gust makes timing itself the resource.

verdict_why: Two real rules gaps remain (which Late units High Pressure holds, and what a lifted enemy counts as); the rest reads cleanly and should not change.

points.text: Lady High Pressure says every waiting Late unit arrives when the Storm breaks, but not whether a Late unit counts as waiting before its normal arrival time; if she dies on attack one, does the Duke land early? Say it.
The Sí Gaoithe doesn't say what happens if the rest of the enemy board dies while its unit is lifted: does the fight end, and does the lifted unit count for hero damage?

Five cards count slightly different things (Gusts; Gusts or Late; different units that Gusted). One shared after-fight tally of Gusts and arrivals on screen would let a player read the Glass, Heron and Tower at a glance.
Mr Fair and Mrs Foul both state the swap; keep the rules only on Mrs Foul and let Mr Fair say 'Mrs Foul takes his place', so the two cards can't drift apart.
Countess Bora's flavour is perfect, but her Late arrival Gust only shows the knock-flat once; a line letting her first Gust knock both neighbours flat would make her arrival feel like a bora.

standouts.why: Sir Vane pointing at the last unit played is the fickle weathercock in one rule, visible on the board, and makes play order matter.
The Duke counting the gap is lightning-to-thunder as a mechanic, and the count reads at a glance.
Mr Fair and Mrs Foul, never home together, is the weather house as a real board-and-hand swap.

weakest.why: Dew-Pond Heron is a generic 'buff your biggest by a count' card with little of the court in it.
Windhover's text is fine but small; the kestrel holding still in the wind could do more than a once-a-fight +1/+1.
The Steward is a bare doubler; the bag of winds deserves a moment, like letting all the winds out at once.

flags.note: Which Late units count as waiting before their normal arrival is unsaid.
With the Steward and goldens, held Gusts go x4 to x9 in one burst; one-sided wipes may feel unfair.
Fight end and hero damage while the lifted enemy is out are unsaid.
With Black Cloud, every revived unit gains +2/+2 permanently; bounded by deaths but worth a look.
Counting enemy attacks makes him much stronger against wide boards.
